summary: Yuto Kawamura works in Indology and linguistics. He served as a postdoctoral fellow at Kyoto University from 2015 to 2018, with posts also attested at Hiroshima University (2013–2020) and the University of Oxford (2019).

Yuzo Mizoguchi (1932–2010) was a scholar of Sinology and philosophy. He studied at the University of Tokyo, Nagoya University, and Kyushu University, later holding posts at Saitama University (~1972–1978), the University of Tokyo (~1978–1993), and Daito Bunka University (~1993–2003).

Zarawar Khan specializes in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He earned an MA and PhD in archaeology from the University of Peshawar and served as Assistant Professor of Archaeology at the University of Swat (attested 2019–2022).

Zeff Bjerken works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies. Educated at UC Santa Barbara and the University of Michigan (PhD 2001) under Donald S. Lopez Jr., he held a post at the College of Charleston (attested 2001).

Zeng Yang works in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He was a research student under Toshinori Ochiai at the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies and completed a PhD at the University of British Columbia under Jinhua Chen (attested 2018).
Zenno Ikuno specializes in Indology and Buddhist studies. He earned an MA from the University of Tokyo and held an attested post at Asia University in 1982.

Zenno Ishigami (1929–2020) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Taisho University (~1949–1953), where he later served as Professor (~1976–2000), and was a researcher at Sanko Research Institute (attested 2008).

Zenryu Tsukamoto (1898–1980) studied Buddhist studies and Sinology at Bukkyo University and Kyoto University. He held posts at the Academy of Oriental Culture (~1929–1949), Kyoto University as President (attested 1956–1966), Bukkyo University (~1961–1971), and Kacho Junior College (~1961–1974).
Zesei Machida worked in Buddhist studies. He served as bettō at Kuon-ji (attested 1990) and as professor emeritus at Minobusan University (attested 1996–2001).
Zhao Luo works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Sinology. He studied under Sen Wang and held a post as a scholar at the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences (attested 2014).
Zhaohua Yang works in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies. He held posts at Stanford University (attested 2007) and Columbia University (faculty, attested 2018).

Zhe Ji specializes in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Sinology. He earned a PhD in sociology from the École des hautes études en sciences sociales in 2007 and was Associate Professor at INALCO (attested 2011–2017).
Zhen Liu specializes in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He completed an MA at Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich in 2005 and an MA at Lanzhou University in 2009.
Zhenhua (1922–2021) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Tianning Buddhist College in 1947 and under Yin Shun in 1952. He served as manager at Fuyan Buddhist Institute (attested 1992).

Zhihua Yao works in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He earned a PhD at Boston University (~1996–2002) under Malcolm David Eckel, served as Professor at the University of Hong Kong (2005), and joined The Chinese University of Hong Kong (~2003).

Zhiru Ng specializes in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Sinology. She earned an MA at the University of Michigan and a PhD at the University of Arizona under Robert M. Gimello, later serving at Pomona College (attested 2007–2014).

Zhiyi Yang (born 1979) specializes in Sinology. After undergraduate studies at Peking University, she earned her PhD at Princeton under Martin Kern, and held positions at the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg and Goethe University Frankfurt (attested 2015).

Zhonghui Cui works in Buddhist studies, history and archaeology, and Sinology. She earned an MA from SOAS University of London, a PhD from the University of Hong Kong, and served as a teaching consultant at the University of Hong Kong (attested 2013).

Zhongxin Jiang (1942–2002) was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Xianlin Ji at Peking University (~1960–1965). He worked at Peking University (~1968–1978) and was Associate Professor at the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences (~1978–2002).
Zijie Li specializes in Buddhist studies. He studied at Komazawa University (attested 2015) and held a DC research fellowship with the Japan Society for the Promotion of Science (attested 2015).
